observation: Structured worklog tools must be the source of truth for this development session; create/activate, render, record meaningful observations, add tasks, update task state, and ensure all tasks are terminal before reporting completion.
Development should prefer TDD/simple solutions, consult the human when specifications are unclear, and avoid unnecessary defensive code or complex fallback logic.
New code should use intention-revealing names, small single-purpose functions/classes, clean formatting, and tests where practical.

This is an Obsidian community plugin using npm/esbuild/TypeScript; source should live in src with main.ts kept minimal, no generated main.js commits, settings/commands should be stable, startup should remain light, and features should avoid network or excessive vault scans.
Project uses npm scripts `test`, `build`, `lint`; Vitest is already configured and strict TypeScript settings include noImplicitReturns and noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

Agent tools are registered in `createObsidianTools(app)` using TypeBox schemas, return `AgentToolResult` via a local `textResult()`, and current vault-scoped tools include read/write/edit/ls/find/grep/get_active_note.

Existing vault utilities handle path normalization, text searching, line slicing, and tool output truncation; task discovery should reuse these conventions for vault-relative paths, markdown file filtering, and truncated output.
Sibling task-properties plugin discovers tasks through Obsidian metadata cache `listItems`, where task status is in `ListItemCache.task`, and reads frontmatter tags to limit work to task notes.

Installed Tasks plugin exposes a plugin instance with `getTasks()` and parses individual lines via an internal `fromLine`; it also treats custom status symbols as task statuses and has a public apiV1 for task line modals/toggling, but no source files are available locally.
Obsidian `ListItemCache.task` is a single-character checkbox status; `' '` is incomplete, any other character is completed, and list item positions use 0-based line/column offsets.

title: Add tested metadataCache task extraction and formatting utilities.

content: Starting metadataCache-based task extraction utilities first so the agent tools can reuse one tested implementation.

Implementing a pure `src/vault/tasks.ts` module that accepts Obsidian cached metadata plus file content. This keeps discovery tied to `metadataCache.listItems` while making extraction/filtering/summarizing easy to unit test without a full Obsidian app mock.

Initial targeted test command `npm test -- --runInBand src/vault/tasks.test.ts` failed because Vitest does not support Jest's `--runInBand` option in this project. Re-running with Vitest's file argument only.

Added `src/vault/tasks.ts` plus `src/vault/tasks.test.ts`. The utility extracts tasks only from `CachedMetadata.listItems` entries with `task` set, reads the cached line text from file content for display/query matching, treats `' '` as todo and every other status symbol as done, preserves parent line numbers where Obsidian exposes them, and formats task lists/summaries.

Validation: `npm test -- src/vault/tasks.test.ts` passes (6 tests). A helper bug around Obsidian's root `parent` value for line 0 was fixed by ignoring self-parent values.
MetadataCache extraction and formatting utilities are implemented and covered by targeted tests.
Starting read-only tool registration for `list_tasks` and `summarize_tasks`, using the metadataCache utilities from task-4.

Registered `list_tasks` and `summarize_tasks` in `createObsidianTools(app)`. Both tools are read-only, accept optional vault-relative `path`, `status`, `query`, and `maxResults`, and discover tasks by iterating `app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` scoped to the target path, reading `app.metadataCache.getFileCache(file).listItems`, and only reading file contents for files whose cache contains task list items.

Added `src/tools/obsidianTools.test.ts` for tool execution against a mocked Obsidian app. Validation: `npm test -- src/tools/obsidianTools.test.ts` passes (2 tests).
Task discovery tools are registered and covered by targeted mocked-app tests.
Starting final guidance update and full validation.

Updated `src/agent/systemPrompt.ts` so the agent prefers `list_tasks` and `summarize_tasks` for task-related questions, noting that they use Obsidian's metadata cache for checkbox task discovery. Running full tests and production build next.
